name: casual
title: Casual SFX Pack
description: Sound effects for hyper-casual and casual mobile web games. Designed to pair with the Super Casual UI Kit.
style: Modern mobile casual game audio: clean, bright, punchy, lightly processed. Not retro/8-bit, not cinematic/orchestral. Mono, dry (no long reverb tails), normalized to -1 dBFS peak.

sourceMeaning.code: Synthesized by the runtime, permanently. No audio file, no download, infinite variation. These sounds are synthetic by nature so code beats a recording.
sourceMeaning.ai: Generated as an audio file (ElevenLabs Sound Effects or similar) from the prompt below. These sounds carry real-world material texture that code cannot fake.
sourceMeaning.hybrid: A coded layer plus a generated layer. The code part ships immediately; the audio part deepens it later.

ui.tap.whenToUse: The player taps any button. The most-used sound in the game.

ui.tap.soft.whenToUse: Secondary taps: list rows, tab switches, small toggles. Quieter than ui.tap.

ui.back.whenToUse: Back, close or cancel. The darker twin of ui.tap.

ui.countdown.whenToUse: 3… 2… 1… before a level starts. Play once per number, then state.go.

ui.go.whenToUse: The GO! at the end of a countdown, when gameplay starts.

ui.slider.whenToUse: A slider handle passes a step. Fires rapidly, so it is very short and quiet.
